title: 15.2 A 1024-Channel 0.00029mm2/ch 74nW/ch Online Spatial Spike-Sorting Chip with Event-Driven Spike Detection and Self-Organizing Map Clustering
problem: High-density multi-electrode arrays (HD-MEA) for brain-computer interfaces generate massive raw spike data that must be reduced on-chip for wireless operation. Prior spike-sorting (SS) designs either require large input buffers, use temporal features that don't scale to multi-channel systems, access entire clustering memory per spike, or consume high power and area.
motivation: Next-gen BCIs require high-channel-count HD-MEA for fine motor/speech decoding and brain understanding, but raw data rates are prohibitive for wireless transmission without on-chip sorting.
method: A 1024-channel spike-sorting chip uses event-driven spike detection (only processes spike events, not raw samples) and spatial spike-sorting (uses waveform shape, not time features) with self-organizing map (SOM) clustering. Event-driven and spatial approaches avoid large buffers, scale to multi-channel systems, and eliminate per-spike full-memory accesses.
key_novelty: Event-driven spike detection + spatial spike-sorting via SOM achieves 1024-channel low-power operation with <50μs latency.
contributions: Event-driven spike detection avoiding large sample buffers
Spatial spike-sorting using waveform features vs. temporal features
Self-organizing map (SOM) clustering with efficient memory access
